summary.short: Virginia's 2026 Special Session I appropriation act (HB 30) levies, from July 1, 2026 to July 1, 2028, an electricity consumption tax on data center operators, with refunds of excess revenue, and adds data center cooling-water, noise, grid and reporting provisions.
summary.long: Virginia's 2026 Special Session I appropriation act (HB 30), covering fiscal years 2027 and 2028, amends the Code and adds data center provisions. From July 1, 2026 to July 1, 2028 it levies an electricity consumption tax of $0.011/kWh per month on each data center operator; revenue above $600,000,000 per fiscal year goes to a non-reverting fund used for refunds from fiscal 2027, administered by the State Corporation Commission. The Department of Environmental Quality must set cooling-water scarcity criteria by July 1, 2027; in designated areas data centers must certify water-saving cooling before July 1, 2032, and new air-permit applicants in the Eastern Virginia Groundwater Management Area after January 1, 2027 must use air, recycled-water, stormwater or closed-loop cooling. DEQ noise regulations apply from December 31, 2029, with civil penalties of up to $32,500 per day from January 1, 2030. The Corporation Commission may weigh economic benefits to disadvantaged communities in large-load interconnection requests, and Phase II utilities' annual incremental strategic undergrounding investment increases are limited to three percent of distribution rate base. Utilities, water providers and agencies report data center contracts, water use and generators by October 1, 2026, and a Joint Subcommittee on Tax Policy studies data center incentives, reporting by December 15, 2026. The act takes effect July 1, 2026; the first enactment expires June 30, 2028.

notes: Excerpt-based annotation: the document omits much of the first enactment and many sections, so relations and entities cover only the excerpted provisions. Possible inconsistency: Part 3 § 3-5.24 para. 2 defines 'data center' on its own terms (facility with at least one megawatt of capacity), while Items 366 and 367 refer to the definition in subdivision A 43 of § 58.1-3506, which is not in this excerpt and is not among the sections listed as amended. Some amended Code sections are listed as both currently effective and as they shall become effective; both are listed but not separately coded. Phase II Utility (a defined class) is not coded as an entity.
